text:
maria: Quick check on the gen API contract — how are we specifying precedence and semantics when stop sequences, max_tokens, and sampling params (temperature/top_p) interact?

maria: Example: client sends max_tokens=1, stop=["\n"], temperature=0.0, top_p=0.9. Do we guarantee the model will return the stop token as the final token and set terminated_by_stop in metadata, or can tokenization/truncation cause a partial token to be dropped?

aj: short answer: stop should win, but there are edge cases if max_tokens cuts mid-token or streaming truncates. we discussed adding explicit semantics earlier. pinging @devon for runtime details. :ear:

devon: We currently apply max_tokens first at the runtime write buffer level, then run stop-checking on each emitted token. If the stop is detected, we terminate the stream and mark terminated_by_stop=true. But if max_tokens limit is hit exactly when a token contains the stop substring (depends on tokenizer splitting), the token may be emitted without us re-checking partial sub-token matches.

nisha: To clarify: do we treat stop matches only on full token boundaries, or do we scan the incremental byte/char stream for substrings? That affects the partial-token drop cases.

devon: We match on the tokenization boundary by default (fast and predictable). We could add an incremental char-scan mode but that's slower and could change determinism.

sam: Related API contract question: what do we guarantee for logprobs when a stop triggers termination? Do we return logprobs for the stop token and any trailing partial tokens? Current tests in ci show we sometimes return null logprobs if termination happened inside a partial token.

maria: Good point. Clients rely on stable logprob presence for downstream scoring. We should define that: if terminated_by_stop, runtime must include the final token's logprob if the token was emitted. If termination prevented token emission, no logprob should be present.

leo: Also we need to be explicit about temperature/top_p interplay: if temperature=0 (greedy) and top_p provided, do we ignore top_p? Currently behavior: temp takes precedence for sampling algorithm selection (temp==0 -> deterministic greedy), and top_p is ignored. That's in the runtime but not in the API docs.

aj: suggest we add a small compatibility matrix in the API spec: rows for (temp==0, temp>0 && top_p set, top_p only, both set but temp small) with described behavior. keep it readable.

nisha: backward-compat note: if we change stop semantics (token vs char matching) we must ship as new minor version or feature flag. Clients relying on exact stop boundaries (eg. eval suites) will break.

devon: Implementation note: if we add char-level stop, we'll provide a config flag stop_mode: ["token_boundary", "substring"]. Default stays token_boundary to preserve current runtime perf. We can allow private beta for substring.

maria: OK. Action items: (1) add the compatibility matrix + explicit logprob semantics to the API docs (PR from docs team), (2) add stop_mode field to the schema and gate it behind a feature flag, (3) add unit tests covering: stop at token boundary, stop as substring across tokens, max_tokens truncation at boundary vs mid-token, streaming termination behavior for logprobs.

sam: I'll open the tests PR. will include examples and a small harness that hits both greedy (temp=0) and sampling cases with top_p and temp combos.

leo: I'll draft the spec text. We should include an example response body snippet demonstrating terminated_by_stop and logprobs arrays. e.g.:

```
{"id":"r-123","choices":[{"text":"Hello\n","logprobs":[-0.1,-0.4],"terminated_by_stop":true}],"model":"open-ish"}
```

aj: ci-bot, is there any flaky test coverage around these cases we should know about?

ci-bot: tests/gen/termination_tests.py:line 42 has an intermittent failure on pod-starved runners, flake rate ~0.6%. Not related to param semantics but will slow CI.

maria: thanks. let's prioritize the spec PR so SDK teams can opt-in. I'll file a ticket for docs + schema change and tag eng-runtime + devex.

nisha: one last ask: verify embedding/length counters used for billing count the emitted tokens only (not stopped partial bytes). otherwise customers will get billed for truncated partial token.

devon: confirmed: billing only counts emitted tokens. we should add that to the billing faq.

maria: perfect. i'll post the ticket and link PRs here. thanks everyone :thumbsup:
